Solicitation

/suh-lis-ih-TAY-shun/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Solicitation means the act of asking for or trying to obtain something, such as support, donations, or business

Solicitation means the act of asking for or trying to obtain something, such as support, donations, or business

Worked Example

The children's hospital's spring <strong style="color:var(--accent);">solicitation</strong> — a mailed letter asking longtime supporters for donations toward a new playroom — raised more money than any campaign in its history.

The letter exists for one purpose: to ask. An organized act of asking supporters for money or help is precisely what a solicitation is.

How Solicitation Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

appeal

appeal: an earnest request for help or support

entreaty

entreaty: a heartfelt, urgent plea

petition

petition: a formal request, often signed by many people

Antonyms

offer

offer: something given or proposed without being asked for

rebuff

rebuff: a blunt rejection of an approach or request

How Strong Is It? — hint → solicitation → supplication

hint vs. solicitation

hint vs. solicitation: A hint only gestures at what you want; a solicitation asks for it openly and on purpose.

supplication vs. solicitation

supplication vs. solicitation: A supplication is far more intense than a solicitation — it is desperate, humble begging.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — solicit-

Root — solicit-: to stir up, ask earnestly (Latin sollicitare, from sollus 'whole' + citare 'to rouse, set in motion')

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: act or process of

Put it together

Put it together: Sollicitare meant 'to stir the whole thing up' — to rouse someone into responding. Add -ation and you get the act of stirring someone to respond: an earnest, deliberate ask.

Use the root in a new word: recite

Use the root in a new word: recite: Each morning the actor would recite his lines in the empty theater — literally 'setting them in motion again' out loud.

Root Check

Word Choice

Formal / business & legal

Solicitation lives in formal territory: 'No Solicitation' signs on office doors, fundraising letters, legal filings about the solicitation of investors. Don't confuse it with the look-alike solicitude, which means anxious concern for someone's well-being — asking versus caring.
